newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Swissair stock dives as 1996 loss looms.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swissair stock dives as 1996 loss looms.

text.p: Shares of Swissair AG plunged on Thursday after the airline warned that it might report a net loss for 1996 due to the continued losses at its Belgian partner Sabena.

Swissair's chairman Hannes Goetz and designated chief executive officer Philippe Bruggisser also unveiled a new corporate holding company structure that reflects a recent aggresive expansion into catering and duty-free business.
Together with its partners Sabena and Austrian Airlines, Swissair also placed a joint order for 17 Airbus A330-200 aircraft including 19 options.

The three European airlines and their U.S. partner Delta Air Lines also announced a tigher cooperation on the hotly-contested North Atlantic routes from February 1, 1997, including revenue sharing, standardised air fares and open reservation systems.

But the stock market gave Swissair's efforts a thumbs down with its shares ending 62 Swiss francs lower, or 5.7 percent at 1,025 francs on disappointment that Swissair had dashed hopes that it would spin-off some of its profitable units or even enter into a new alliance with another airline.
"The surprise was that there was no surprise," said Urs Kunz of Credit Suisse.
Despite the deteriorating airline business in October and November, Bruggisser said he still aims to fulfil his goals.
"The aim is still to break even in flight operations in 1997 -- our new structures will make it easier to see -- and we will attempt to reach that," Bruggisser told a news conference.
In 1995 Swissair posted a net loss of 147 million francs ($110 million), but largely due to restructuring charges of 365 million that hid an improvement in its operating results.

But while the improvement continued in the first six months of this year -- the first half loss narrowed to 51 million francs from 86 million -- Swissair's airline business encountered a "deeply disappointing October" due to higher fuel prices and less-than-expected traffic.
Swissair's Bruggisser, who will become chief executive on January 1, cautioned that the group's operating result for 1996 could fall below 1995's 237 million francs.
"A decline in operating result was not a great surprise," said Giorgio Cortiana of Union Bank of Switzerland.
However, business at Sabena, in which Swissair has a 49.5 percent stake, is worse than anticipated.
"Without a Sabena write-down, Swissair would show a profit," Cortiana added.

Sabena, which already made a loss in the first half of 1996 is expected to record another loss for the second half of this year and Swissair is considering writing down the value of its stake in Sabena, which it bought for 270 million francs.
"Needless to say, any value adjustment of this kind would lead to a corresponding reduction in group profit for the year, and could concievably push that result into the red," Bruggisser said.

Bruggisser, known to have opposed Swissair's acquisition of the stake in Sabena, noted that Swissair probably should have paid less for its stake in Sabena, which is still trying to recoup from a series of cripling strikes earlier this year.

Swissair's management will propose to shareholders the creation of a new, pure holding company -- to be named SAirGroup -- which will become an umbrella that covers four sub-holding companies that reflect the group's four main activities: airlines, catering, cargo/logistics and services.

While the Swissair name will continue to exist, the adoption of a new structure and a new name for the holding company reflects that Swissair has evolved into a diversified group with the core flying activity -- still in the red -- is surrounded by a variety of profitable activities, such as catering.
"We want to communicate the fact that our group has grown into much more than just an airline," Goetz said, noting that Swissair wants to offer an integrated travel service.
The move reflects Swissair's view that travellers no longer solely judge an airline by the flight itself, but also by ground services, inflight meals and general comfort level on board.
-- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($1=1.3348 Swiss Franc)
